text:
alex: quick heads-up — microbench on pr-9123 shows ~18% mem increase on 4k sequences vs main. attaching bench artifacts: https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/9123/artifacts :eyes:

maria: uh ok, can you paste the exact config you ran? was this with quant fallback or the new allocator change?

alex: ran with --profile microbatch --seq 4096 --batch 8 --quant=nvh --allocator=dynamic

alex: command:
```
bench run --profile microbatch --tag pr-9123 --seq 4096 --batch 8 --quant nvh --allocator dynamic 
```

jin: thanks. saw the bench-bot summary? bench-bot, drop the perf diff here please.

bench-bot: SUMMARY for pr-9123 vs main:
- p95 latency: +2%
- throughput: -1.5%
- max RSS (4k, batch8): +18% (1.2GB -> 1.42GB)
- note: GC churn increased on step ~150
artifact: https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/9123/summary.json

tim: if GC churn is up that suggests extra allocations per token or a cache miss pattern. alex, any code paths that touch KV layout or prefill here?

alex: PR touches prefill eviction heuristics and a tiny change in tensor scratch allocation ordering. the allocator reorder was meant to reduce fragmentation but might be causing extra copies in the prefill hotpath.

maria: could you run a micro trace with env DEBUG_ALLOC=1 to capture allocation stack traces? also try main with same env to make sure baseline matches bench-bot.

alex: on it. running trace now, will post when done. ETA ~20m.

jin: adding a review note: if this is allocator-related we should hold the canary until we either revert or add a guard flag. we have a scheduled deploy window at 11:30 PT but this looks risky.

maria: @alex also ping reviewers: @jin @tim we need at least one more approval for the allocator change. can we prioritize?

alex: requesting quick approvals on github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9123 — left a small repro in the description.

tim: looking now. quick reading: allocator reorder is gated by env var ALLOC_DYNAMIC=false/true? iirc default is true in canary. we could flip default to false until we verify.

alex: yes it's behind config flag but our canary uses true by default. i can make a follow-up to default-opt-out and add runtime telemetry for alloc copy counts.

jin: agree that's safest. would prefer a short revert to avoid customer exposure, but default flip is fine if it's quick. alex, do you have a patch ready?

alex: pushing a tiny patch to set default to false and add a telemetry counter. PR #9130. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9130

maria: thanks. once #9130 lands we should rerun the same microbench (same flags) and confirm mem delta goes away. can bench-bot auto-run and report?

bench-bot: queued rerun for pr-9130, will post results here when done. job id 88721. ETA ~18m.

tim: if bench-bot confirms then we can proceed with canary window after a short smoke. otherwise revert. also add a regression note to the PR describing the mem bump and the artifacts.

alex: noted. adding regression section now.

maria: quick ask for reviewers: please post approvals/comments in the PR thread so we have audit trail. :thumbsup:

jin: ack, i'll review and leave comments by EOD.

bench-bot: RERUN COMPLETE for job 88721:
- p95 latency: +1.9%
- throughput: -0.8%
- max RSS (4k, batch8): +2% (1.2GB -> 1.22GB)
- delta largely within noise envelope
link: https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/88721/report.html

alex: looks like default flip fixes most of the gap. I'll merge #9130 after CI and mark the canary as safe to continue. thanks all for quick turnaround. :rocket:

maria: follow-up: please add a short note to the release docs mentioning the allocator reordering as opt-in and the telemetry we added so SRE can track.

alex: will do.

tim: great. once merged let's run a 30m smoke on staging to watch memory and tail p95.

alex: scheduling smoke job now. I'll ping here with results.

bench-bot: scheduled smoke: job 88745.
